caption:
You already know what happens next. That is the whole trick.

An anticipation hook is a shot of something one second away from resolving — and your brain refuses to scroll until it sees the ending. It does not have to relate to your topic at all. It buys you the three seconds you need.

Three in this video:

→ The first domino, already past the point of no return
→ One block holding a whole tower
→ A glass more off the table than on it

Why it works: Instagram ranks on watch time, and the first three seconds decide whether anyone reaches your actual point. Mosseri has said about half of Instagram videos are watched with no sound, so the hook has to work on mute — movement and tension in frame one, not a clever line.

How to use it: put 2–3 seconds of the hook at the very front, then cut hard into your real content. The tension carries the viewer across the cut.

One warning, and it matters more than it used to. Do not lift someone else's clip. Instagram removes accounts from recommendations after 10+ reposts of other people's content in 30 days. Film it yourself or build it — every hook in this video was made from scratch.
